market_name: Will 3 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm the market probability moved on genuine flow, not a single mispriced trade; check 2y/10y Treasury yields and Fed funds futures for corroboration.
time_plan.1h: Check whether SOFR/fed funds futures and short-end yields have echoed the move; look for any Fed speak or data release explaining it.
time_plan.2h: Re-assess TLT vs the size of the yield move; verify the repricing is persisting rather than mean-reverting.
time_plan.6h: Compare against equity and dollar behavior for consistency of a dovish narrative; watch for scheduled data (CPI, jobs) that could dominate.
time_plan.12h: Evaluate whether the dovish shift held into the close; note if move faded (suggesting noise) for calibration.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 3 Fed cuts in 2026 signals a more dovish rate-path expectation. Lower expected policy rates pull down the whole yield curve, especially the long end, lifting long-duration bond prices. TLT is the most liquid direct proxy for this repricing.

predictions.tradable_instrument_name: Invesco DB US Dollar Index Bullish Fund

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check DXY and major pairs (EURUSD, USDJPY) for confirmation the dollar is softening alongside the rate-cut repricing.
time_plan.1h: Verify no offsetting risk-off flow (which can support USD despite dovish Fed) is dominating.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether rate-differential logic or safe-haven demand is driving the dollar.
time_plan.6h: Watch for foreign central bank news or US data that could swamp the Fed-path signal.
time_plan.12h: Judge whether the dollar's move aligned with the dovish thesis; flag weak proxy if no consistent move.

predictions.reasoning: More expected Fed cuts narrow US rate differentials versus other currencies, typically weakening the dollar. UUP is a liquid proxy that would drift lower on a dovish repricing, though FX is driven by many cross-currents and the link is weaker than for Treasuries.

evidence_used: Market question tracks number of 25bp Fed cuts in 2026, a direct read on expected monetary policy path
Standard macro linkages: dovish rate expectations lower yields (bonds up), weaken USD, and tend to lift gold and equities
Liquidity of TLT and UUP as tradable proxies for rate-path and dollar views
uncertainty_notes: The 700bp tradability threshold is far above realistic 12h moves in these liquid rate/FX proxies; direction may be right but magnitude is small
A probability move in the market may already reflect public data (e.g., CPI, FOMC minutes) and thus be priced into assets
Mislabeled primary topic ('military_conflict') suggests metadata noise; the question itself is clearly monetary policy
Safe-haven flows can decouple USD from rate differentials, and long-end yields can move on term-premium/fiscal factors unrelated to Fed path

llm_justification.summary: This is a US monetary-policy market: a sharp rise in the implied probability of 3 Fed cuts in 2026 reflects a more dovish rate-path expectation. The cleanest public-market implications are lower Treasury yields (TLT up) and a softer dollar (UUP down). Directions are defensible but expected 12h magnitudes are far below the 700bp tradable threshold, so these are low-conviction, non-tradable research mappings rather than actionable signals.
key_assumptions: A move in this market represents a genuine shift in expected Fed policy, not thin-market noise
Standard rate-differential and duration linkages hold over the 12h window
The repricing is not already fully reflected in bond and FX markets
failure_modes: Move reverses as thin prediction-market liquidity mean-reverts
The dovish shift was already public (post-data or post-FOMC) and thus priced into TLT/UUP
USD proxy is weakly exposed if risk-off haven demand offsets the rate-differential effect
Long-end yields driven by term premium/fiscal supply rather than Fed path, breaking the TLT link
Magnitudes stay well under 700bps, making any 'signal' untradable under the stated rule
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
